I'm working through the first question, starting with the root केव् (to serve, ātmanepadī, bhvādi class), needing to form it through यङ् then णिच् then लुङ् in कर्तरि प्रयोग, parasmaipada, madhyamapuruṣa dvivacana, combined with the prefix वि. I'm building the reduplicated यङ् form, working out the guṇa of the abhyāsa.

Continuing this, I'm applying 7.4.59 to shorten the abhyāsa vowel from ए to इ, then guṇa gives ए back, yielding चेकेव्य. Then adding णिच्, I'm using 6.4.49 (यस्य हलः) to delete the य since it follows a consonant, arriving at चेकेवि — since the उपधा ए is guru, no further guṇa applies. Now moving to लुङ् with चङ् per णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्, I'm deleting the णि (अनिट्) to get चेकेव्+अ, and considering how reduplication under 6.1.11 interacts with the already-reduplicated यङ् stem.

For the dvitva again, I'm thinking of the parallel case बोभूय + णिच् + लुङ् giving अबोभवत् as a known reference form, trying to recall why no further reduplication occurs — pointing to Siddhānta Kaumudī's treatment of ण्यन्त यङ्लुक् forms in लुङ्.

I'm trying to pin down why अपिपठिषत् doesn't get doubly reduplicated — the "एकाचो द्वे प्रथमस्य" rule seems to apply only once to the first syllable, blocking a second reduplication in the derivation chain.

Working through the yaṅanta-ṇijanta case for bhū similarly: bobhūya + ṇic goes through lopa of the vowel, and under लुङ् with णेरनिटि the expected form comes out as अबोभूयत्. This seems consistent with how these generated verb-form questions are typically structured, likely mirroring an automated Sanskrit paradigm generator.

Now I'm checking whether सन्वद्भाव applies to the existing abhyāsa के — since के is guru rather than laghu, the rule requiring a laghu element after the abhyāsa doesn't trigger, so sanvadbhāva doesn't apply here. I'm also weighing whether उपधा ह्रस्व under णौ चङ्यु applies to this form.

This confirms the pattern - चित् gives अचीचितत्, so upadhā shortening ए→इ indeed applies. Applying this to चेकेव्, the णौ चङ्युपधाया ह्रस्वः rule should turn it into चेकिव्, and I'm checking whether there's any अग्लोप-type restriction blocking this since the णि has been elided but remains sthānivat for this purpose.

Since 1.1.57 only applies sthānivat status for an ādeśa conditioned by a following element when it affects something preceding, I'm checking whether अतो लोपः qualifies — the deleted अ was conditioned by the following आर्धधातुक णिच्, so it should count as sthānivat, meaning the upadhā would effectively still be अ-adjacent rather than ए. But यस्य हलः removing य is a separate hal-deletion not covered by that sthānivat rule, so I need to work out how the two interact for upadhā-hrasva.

I recall the Siddhāntakaumudī explanation that यस्य हलः refers to the whole य (saṅghāta) being deleted after a consonant in ārdhadhātuka contexts, like बेभिदिता, but I'm unsure whether this counts as sthānivat since the sthānī technically includes an ac, which complicates applying 1.1.57. I'm trying to recall a concrete example involving yaṅanta plus ṇic plus luṅ to test this.

Looking at कथ → कथयति, I'm recalling that the अ-lopa isn't treated as sthānivat for upadhā vṛddhi purposes, which is why there's no vṛddhi there — trying to see if the same logic applies to the यस्य हलः case.

I'm checking the list of exceptions where sthānivat doesn't apply, but yalopa there refers to operations on the lopa itself, not the result — that doesn't quite match this case. I'm also wondering whether this question comes from an automated derivation system like vidyut, and what it would output for yaṅanta plus ṇic in luṅ, though I'm not certain of its exact behavior here.

So I'm working through the Pāṇinian derivation of केव् by hand: forming the yaṅ reduplicated stem चेकेव्य through dvitva, abhyāsa rules, guṇa, and cuṭu substitution, then applying ṇic with the hetumat sense, tracking where the final अ is lost and where य is deleted according to the Siddhāntakaumudī's ordering of rules.

Then adding चङ् with णि-lopa gives चेकेव् + अ + तम्. Now I need to check 7.4.-type rule for चङि उपधा shortening: is the upadhā of चेकेव् before णि short ए or इ, depending on whether the earlier लोप is sthānivat — if यस्य हलः deletion counts as removing the whole य unit including its अ, that affects whether this rule even applies.

I'm testing this against the analogous अदन्त root कथ: कथ + णिच् → अतो लोपः deletes the अ, then उपधा वृद्धि is blocked by sthānivat, giving कथि, and in लुङ् चङ् the उपधा stays short because "अग्लोपित्वान्न सन्वद्भावः" applies, giving अचकथत्.

I'm also checking ऊनयति: ऊन + णिच् → ऊन्+इ, and in लुङ् with reduplication the उपधा ऊ unexpectedly stays unshortened in औनिनत्, which I'm attributing to sthānivat again.

So since अ is sthānivat, the upadhā remains न्, meaning no hrasva applies here. Working through the reduplication, I'm tracing how औनिनत् forms, with dvitva occurring on the "नि" portion before णि-lopa, since अग्लोपी blocks the sanvadbhāva that would otherwise interfere.

Now I'm questioning whether this same sthānivat principle for अ-lopa extends to यङ् forms too — whether the lopa there happens via अतो लोपः or through यस्य हलः governing the whole, and if that deletion counts as sthānivat, recalling the classical discussion around बेभिदि as a test case.

By आदेः परस्य, only the initial य् is deleted, then अतो लोपः removes the अ, and this अ-lopa counts as sthānivat so laghūpadha guṇa doesn't apply—giving बेभिदिता not बेभेदिता. Extending this to यङन्त forms like चेकेव्य+णिच्, the deleted अ being sthānivat means upadhā hrasva in luṅ wouldn't trigger on the resulting ए either, since the final letter is treated as if it's still there.

Checking 1.1.57 pūrvavidhi validity: since 7.4.1 operates on the upadhā preceding the lopa'd अ, sthānivat does apply, so the condition is evaluated with अ present and hrasva is blocked—upadhā remains व् which can't undergo hrasva anyway, so the form stays चेकेव्. I'm now moving to work out the dvitva for the चङ् form, reduplicating the first ekāc of the root per 6.1.11.

But I'm questioning whether there's a second round of reduplication needed, thinking about parallel cases like सन्नन्त + णिच् + लुङ् such as अपिपठिषत्, which doesn't show further reduplication—trying to recall the specific paribhāṣā or Mahābhāṣya discussion that blocks additional dvitva in these layered causative-desiderative-aorist formations.

Tracing through bōbhūya formation for bhū with ṇic and luṅ, I work out that the reduplication plus guṇa blocking leads to अबोभूयत्. I'm now recalling that there's a paribhāṣā about reduplication occurring only once, which may be what's governing why these forms don't double up further.

So the derivation I arrive at for vi+cekī in luṅ gives व्यचेकेवतम्, and I need to check whether the सन्वद्भाव rule applies to the abhyāsa given the अक्-लोप in the aṅga here.

Now moving to the second word: श्विदिँ (श्विद् श्वैत्ये, आत्मनेपदी, भ्वादि, इदित् so it takes नुम् giving श्विन्द्). I'm building the yaṅ→णिच्→सन् chain for आशीर्लिङ् कर्तरि परस्मैपद मध्यमपुरुष बहुवचन with प्र, starting from श्विन्द्+यङ् and applying नुम् to the dhātu.

Working through the reduplication: हलादिः शेषः leaves only the first consonant, giving शि as the abhyāsa, then गुण converts it to शे, forming शेश्विन्द्य. Checking whether नुम् survives — since श्विन्द् is इदित्, the नुम् isn't dropped, so I arrive at शेश्विन्द्य and I'm now verifying the nasal placement as अनुस्वार, getting to श्वेश्विन्द्य.

Adding णिच् next: the य् after द् causes अतो लोपः by sthānivadbhāva, giving शेश्विन्द् + इ, and since the उपधा न् isn't a light vowel, no गुण applies — the form stays as शेश्विन्दि. Then adding सन्: since this is a णिजन्त root, the सन्यक् rule requires इट् (parallel to भावयति → बिभावयिषति), so I'm building शेश्विन्दि + इ + स...

Working through गुण (इ→ए→अय्) gives शेश्विन्दयिष, and I'm now questioning whether द्वित्व applies a second time for सन् here — since the root is already reduplicated from णिच्, by analogy with बोभूय+णिच्+सन् forms like बोभूययिषति, I conclude there's no additional reduplication, yielding शेश्विन्दयिषति. I'm trying to recall whether there's a specific वार्त्तिक governing सन्नन्त of यङन्त-णिजन्त roots that confirms this.

Testing this against known examples: जुगुप्स् (from गुप्+सन्) takes सन् again to form जुगुप्सिषते, not जुजुगुप्सिषते, which supports the rule against a second reduplication — similarly मीमांसिषते and लोलूयिषते follow this pattern.

For the madhyama-bahu form, I'm working through the sandhi: थ becomes त via तस्थस्थमिपां, then यासुट् gets added since this is ārdhadhātuka, and लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य removes the non-final स् from the यासुट्-सुट् combination, leaving something like शेश्विन्दयिष्यात.

Actually I realize that स-lopa rule only applies to sārvadhātuka liṅ, not āśīrliṅ — so the स् stays, giving भूयास्त as my model. Also checking iṭ-āgama: since यास्त begins with य, which falls outside the वल् pratyāhāra, no iṭ is needed. So combining शेश्विन्दयिष् with यास्त gives शेश्विन्दयिष्यास्त, and with the प्र prefix: प्रशेश्विन्दयिष्यास्त.

Now I need to check for ṇatva — the न् in श्विन्द् could theoretically turn into ण् due to the र in प्र, but the intervening श् blocks this since it's not in the अट् pratyāhāra permitted for cross-over. I'm also considering whether that न् is actually नुम् and needs to become anusvāra before द् by नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि, then parasavarna to न्.

So no ṇatva applies. For the सन् सुट्, the स् after इ becomes ष् by the आदेशप्रत्यययोः rule, giving इष. So my second answer comes together as प्रशेश्विन्दयिष्यास्त, and I'm verifying the abhyāsa for the yaṅ form of श्विद् is शेश्विन्द्यते, keeping only श् in reduplication with गुण of इ to शे. Then I want to revisit my first question about केवृँ.

Confirming केवृ as the Bhvādi ātmanepadī root meaning "to serve," I work through its forms: यङ् चेकेव्यते, ṇic चेकेवयति, luṅ अचेकेवत्, middle dual अचेकेवतम्, and with वि prefix व्यचेकेवतम्. I'm weighing whether 7.4.1's upadhā-hrasva applies through sthānivat treatment for yaṅ-ṇic combinations — if sthānivat doesn't apply, the form would instead be व्यचेकिवतम्, but following the Siddhāntakaumudī's explicit statement that sthānivat blocks the लघूपधगुण rule here, I'll settle on व्यचेकेवतम् as correct.
